note: Turks and Caicos Islands, read on the Ministry of Border Control and Employment's Work Permits page (gov.tc/bordercontrol) and its work permit fee schedule (Immigration Regulations 2016, as the page serves it) on 2026-10-30. There are three kinds of work permit: employed (skilled and unskilled), self-employed and freelancer. An employed person's application is submitted by the employer (or an accredited agent), to the Work Permit Board of the employer's zone, with the employment contract, the job description and newspaper advertisements, after a labour clearance; a new application is needed on a change of employer, which carries the repatriation fee (work for the sponsor). Each application asks proof of legal entry and lawful stay 'if on island', so it may be made for a worker on the islands or abroad (either). A permit may be asked for several years at once, up to 5 for skilled and 3 for unskilled employed persons; these are ceilings, so no term is kept; renewal applications have their own document list (renewable). The service standard is a labour clearance within 10 working days and the work permit within 25 days where a clearance is needed (kept; the page doesn't say whether these are working days). The annual work permit fee depends on the occupation (Entertainer/Comedian US$2,700, Musician US$1,350, Dancer US$400 in the 2016 schedule, plus the US$150 administrative fee or 10%), so no single fee is kept. Spouses of Turks and Caicos Islanders and permanent residents 'with endorsement to work' work without a work permit; the Permanent Residence Certificate's page didn't answer (404), so no permanent route is written; naturalisation is the citizenship engine's.

sources.said: There are three types of work permit. ... Only Self Employed Person’s and Freelancer’s work permit applications are eligible to be submitted by an employee. All other applications must be submitted by the employer or by agencies/firms accredited to do so on their behalf. ... If on island, proof of legal entry and lawful stay in the Islands ... Employment Contract ... RENEWAL APPLICATION ... Employed - Skilled up to 5 years ... Unskilled up to 3 years ... A non-refundable Repatriation Fee for each first time work permit application and/or upon a new work permit application involving a change in employer. ... Our service standard is to decide a labour clearance, if needed, within 10 working days and work permits within 15 days if a labour clearance is NOT needed and a work permit within 25 days if a clearance is needed. ... A Permanent Resident with endorsement to work
